prompt.en: Gardeners cut the top of a hedge to make it bushy, and the grass on a cricket ground grows back after it is mowed. Explain how each of these plants can grow again after its tips are removed.

label.en: Hedge: new branches from the nodes

level1.en: After the tip of a stem is cut, where on the stem do new branches come from?

clue.en: Leaves and branches arise at nodes, and buds at the nodes grow into new branches.

level2Template.en: When the tip of a hedge stem is cut, new branches grow from the ___ of the stem.

label.en: Grass: intercalary meristem near the base

level1.en: Which meristem is left in a grass stem after its top is cut, and where is it?

clue.en: Grass has a meristem at the nodes of its stem, near the base, that keeps making new cells.

level2Template.en: Grass grows back because the ___ meristem at the nodes near its base keeps making new cells.

text.en: When the stem tips are cut, buds at the nodes grow into new branches, so the hedge becomes bushy.
The intercalary meristem at the nodes near the base of the grass keeps making new cells, so the grass grows back.
